gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: The page requires only that q not divide a denominator (q must not divide ξ). Nothing says why numerators avoid q, and 'the finitely many matrices used' are not identified until the network paragraph. The shear also applies the inverses F1^{-1} and F2^{-1} to fields, and this claim does not establish that their denominators are prime to q.

Tracing the three operations just given: D becomes ζ+η; the swap gives H = ζ+η and D = η; then D becomes η-(ζ+η) = -ζ. The pair becomes (η+ζ, -ζ), not (η+ζ, ζ), so the stated result and the later claim that D is unchanged do not follow.

gaps.quote: So the shear needs $2\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: The page says each update takes one interchange, and there is one update per 1 in Π, where Π has rank_Q M ones. That gives rank_Q M interchanges, not twice that. The page gives no source for the second interchange, and the network paragraph later counts one interchange per unit of rank.

gaps.term: linear cost of a lower-triangular transformation
gaps.note: This cited cost is the mechanism behind the shear's O(V) work. The reader has not studied tape-level data-movement algorithms, and the following sentences argue only in terms of combinations of coordinates. They do not say how coordinates stored at different tape positions are combined in linear time on the fixed-tape machine, or what the cost counts.
